title: Finite reduced dynamics, memory and quantum trajectories

items.title: Finite channel families, semigroups, and CP-divisibility
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $d\geq1$ and let $\Phi_t:M_d(\mathbb C)\to M_d(\mathbb C)$ be a family of finite quantum channels indexed by $t\geq0$, where “finite quantum channel” has the meaning in [[def-qsm-dt-channel-definition]]. The family obeys the **semigroup law** when $\Phi_0=\operatorname{id}_{M_d(\mathbb C)}$ and $\Phi_{t+s}=\Phi_t\circ\Phi_s$ for every $s,t\geq0$.

The family is **CP-divisible** when for every $0\leq s\leq t$ there exists a finite quantum channel $V_{t,s}:M_d(\mathbb C)\to M_d(\mathbb C)$ such that $\Phi_t=V_{t,s}\circ\Phi_s$. CP-divisibility is this specified factorization property; the definition does not assert that it is a universal meaning of “Markovian”.

references.title: Lin Lin and Nathan Wiebe, Quantum Algorithms for Scientific Computation, Chapter 21, §21.1
references.locator: Equations (21.3)–(21.5), printed pp. 307–308: the norm-continuous channel-semigroup convention, cited as a contrast; this local definition retains the algebraic semigroup and CP-divisibility properties without adding continuity.

references.title: Ángel Rivas, Susana F. Huelga, and Martin B. Plenio, Quantum Non-Markovianity: Characterization, Quantification and Detection, §3.2
references.locator: Definition 3.2 and equation (29), printed pp. 10–11: completely positive divisible quantum evolution.

items.title: Continuous finite-dimensional ordered-simplex integrals
items.design_state: Step 2 owner-authorized same-pair local proof; source release recorded, ordinary native gates pending.
items.statement:
Let $T\geq0$, let $n\geq0$ be an integer, and let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real or complex vector space with a specified finite ordered basis and its coordinate topology. Put $D_n(T)=\{0\leq s_1\leq\cdots\leq s_n\leq T\}$, with $D_0(T)=\{()\}$. Let $F:D_n(T)\to V$ have continuous coordinates. Set $G_0=F$. For $1\leq k\leq n$, write $y=(s_{k+1},\ldots,s_n)\in D_{n-k}(T)$ and put $b_k(y)=s_{k+1}$ if $k<n$, and $b_n(())=T$. Define recursively
$$
G_k(y)=\int_0^{b_k(y)}G_{k-1}(s_k,y)\,ds_k,
$$
integrating real coordinates, and real and imaginary parts of complex coordinates. Every integral exists and every $G_k$ is continuous on its remaining parameter domain. Write $I_n(F)=G_n(())$; equivalently this is the iterated integral with limits $0\leq s_1\leq\cdots\leq s_n\leq T$. Degenerate one-variable integrals are zero. For $n=0$, set $I_0(F)=F(())$; for $n\geq1$ and $T=0$, $I_n(F)=0$.

These integrals are linear, independent of the chosen finite basis, and commute with finite-dimensional linear maps. For any norm $\|\cdot\|$ on $V$, the corresponding one-variable integral satisfies $\|\int_a^b g(s)\,ds\|\leq\int_a^b\|g(s)\|\,ds$ for continuous $g$ and $a\leq b$. If $\|F(s)\|\leq C$ on $D_n(T)$, where $C\geq0$, then
$$
\|I_n(F)\|\leq C\frac{T^n}{n!}.
$$
Here the factor for $n=0$ is $1$, including $T=0$. For scalar $F=1$, $I_n(1)=T^n/n!$ with this convention. For real scalar $F\geq0$, every partial integral $G_k$ is nonnegative. No differentiability of $F$ or choice principle is assumed.

references.title: Riemann integration and affine substitution
references.locator: The existing pinned scalar integration suppliers are used below; the parameter-continuity and ordered-simplex argument is proved locally, without new external full-text reading.

items.title: Finite GKSL jump-trajectory branches
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $d\geq1$, let $r\geq0$ be an integer, let $H=H^*\in M_d(\mathbb C)$ have units joules, let $\hbar>0$ have units joule-seconds, and let $L_1,\ldots,L_r\in M_d(\mathbb C)$ have units $\mathrm{s}^{-1/2}$, with the finite GKSL convention of [[def-qsm-dt-gksl-definition]]. Put $K=-iH/\hbar-\frac12\sum_{a=1}^rL_a^*L_a$ and $R(u)=e^{uK}$ for $u\geq0$, with the exponential defined by its norm-convergent power series. For a density matrix $\rho\in M_d(\mathbb C)$, meaning $\rho=\rho^*\geq0$ and $\operatorname{Tr}\rho=1$, define the no-jump branch at time $t\geq0$ by $W_{\varnothing,\varnothing}(t)=R(t)$ and its branch state by $W_{\varnothing,\varnothing}(t)\rho W_{\varnothing,\varnothing}(t)^*$.

All time variables $u,t,s_1,\ldots,s_n$ are measured in seconds. For $n\geq1$, a jump-history label is $\mathbf a=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\in\{1,\ldots,r\}^n$ and its jump times are seconds $0<s_1<\cdots<s_n<t$. Define the corresponding branch operator by $W_{\mathbf a,\mathbf s}(t)=R(t-s_n)L_{a_n}R(s_n-s_{n-1})\cdots L_{a_2}R(s_2-s_1)L_{a_1}R(s_1)$ and the unnormalized branch state by $W_{\mathbf a,\mathbf s}(t)\rho W_{\mathbf a,\mathbf s}(t)^*$. Its branch-weight density is the real-valued scalar function $w_{\mathbf a,\mathbf s}(t)=\operatorname{Tr}(W_{\mathbf a,\mathbf s}(t)\rho W_{\mathbf a,\mathbf s}(t)^*)$. For $n\geq1$, let $\overline{\Delta}_n(t)=\{(s_1,\ldots,s_n)\in\mathbb R^n:0\leq s_1\leq\cdots\leq s_n\leq t\}$ and $\Delta_n(t)=\{(s_1,\ldots,s_n)\in\mathbb R^n:0<s_1<\cdots<s_n<t\}$. Use the same formula for $W_{\mathbf a,\mathbf s}(t)$ on $\overline{\Delta}_n(t)$; it is continuous there because $R(u)=e^{uK}$ is continuous for $u\geq0$. If $V$ is a finite-dimensional real or complex vector space and $F:\overline{\Delta}_n(t)\to V$ has continuous coordinates in a basis, define $\int_{\Delta_n(t)}F(\mathbf s)\,d\mathbf s$ as exactly the repeated one-variable Riemann integral over the closed limits shown here $\int_0^t ds_n\int_0^{s_n}ds_{n-1}\cdots\int_0^{s_2}F(s_1,\ldots,s_n)\,ds_1$, integrating each real coordinate; for complex coordinates, integrate their real and imaginary parts separately. This value is independent of the basis because a change of basis is a finite linear combination and scalar Riemann integration is linear. For $V=\mathbb R$ this defines the scalar integral of the density $w_{\mathbf a,\mathbf s}(t)$; the same convention applies to branch-state integrands with values in $M_d(\mathbb C)$ and to integrands with values in the finite-dimensional complex vector space of complex-linear maps $M_d(\mathbb C)\to M_d(\mathbb C)$. The full recursion is well-defined for these arbitrary continuous integrands by [[lem-nrqmx-continuous-simplex-integrals]]: every inner integral is continuous in all remaining ordered parameters, so the next integral exists. That lemma also proves basis independence, linear-map commutation, the norm bound by the supremum times $t^n/n!$, and positivity for nonnegative real scalar integrands. Set $\int_a^a f(s)\,ds=0$ for a degenerate interval; hence every $n\geq1$ ordered-simplex integral at $t=0$ is zero. Let $\Delta_0(t)=\{()\}$ and define $\int_{\Delta_0(t)}F=F(())$; in the expansion, the $n=0$ contribution is the no-jump branch already defined above. For $n\geq1$, $W_{\mathbf a,\mathbf s}$ has units $\mathrm{s}^{-n/2}$ and $w_{\mathbf a,\mathbf s}$ has units $\mathrm{s}^{-n}$; integrating over the $n$ time variables gives a dimensionless weight. If $r=0$, there are no branches with $n\geq1$. This definition alone does not assert that the branch weights sum to one.

references.title: Lin Lin and Nathan Wiebe, Quantum Algorithms for Scientific Computation, Chapter 21, §21.1
references.locator: Equation (21.1), printed p. 307: the finite GKSL generator and its jump-operator terms; the ordered branch construction here is defined locally.

items.title: Finite system-environment and Markov model assignments
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Work with finite-dimensional system and environment spaces $H_S=\mathbb C^d$ and $H_E=\mathbb C^m$, where $d,m\geq1$, using the ordered tensor product $H_S\otimes H_E$ with the system factor first. A system or environment state is a positive semidefinite Hermitian matrix of trace one; these state matrices are dimensionless. At the initial time, for every allowed system state $\rho$, adopt the joint preparation $\rho\otimes\eta$, where the fixed environment state $\eta$ does not depend on $\rho$. For each $t\geq0$, choose a declared unitary $U_t$ on $H_S\otimes H_E$, meaning $U_t^*U_t=U_tU_t^*=I$, with $U_0=I$. The reduced system dynamics is the map $\Phi_t(\rho)=\operatorname{Tr}_E\!\left(U_t(\rho\otimes\eta)U_t^*\right)$, where for the fixed product basis the finite partial trace has entries $(\operatorname{Tr}_E R)_{\alpha\beta}=\sum_{j=1}^mR_{(\alpha,j),(\beta,j)}$. This assignment excludes initially correlated joint states. It imposes no one-parameter group, continuity, or semigroup law on $U_t$.

A time-homogeneous finite GKSL model may instead be selected as a separate approximation: choose a fixed finite-dimensional Hamiltonian matrix $H=H^*$ in joules, a constant $\hbar>0$ in joule-seconds, and finitely many jump matrices $L_a$ in $\mathrm{s}^{-1/2}$, and use $T_t=e^{t\mathcal L}$ for $t\geq0$ with $\mathcal L(X)=-\frac{i}{\hbar}[H,X]+\sum_a\left(L_aXL_a^*-\frac12\{L_a^*L_a,X\}\right)$. Here $\mathcal L:M_d(\mathbb C)\to M_d(\mathbb C)$ is complex-linear, $[A,B]=AB-BA$, $\{A,B\}=AB+BA$, and $A^*$ is conjugate transpose. The exponential means $e^{t\mathcal L}:=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}t^n\mathcal L^n/n!$, with $\mathcal L^0=\operatorname{id}$ and powers given by composition. This series converges absolutely in the operator norm induced by the finite matrix trace norm $\|X\|_1=\operatorname{Tr}\sqrt{X^*X}$, as in the finite GKSL semigroup theorem cited below; its hypotheses are exactly the finite Hermitian $H$, positive $\hbar$, and finite jump family specified here. Each application must state its rates and physical regime. Selecting this approximation is not a consequence of the finite unitary reduction, and this postulate claims no weak-coupling or reservoir limit.

In both alternatives, the parameter $t$ indexing $U_t$ or $T_t$ denotes elapsed physical time measured in SI seconds. Thus $t\mathcal L$ in the GKSL exponential is dimensionless, since the adopted finite GKSL generator has units $\mathrm{s}^{-1}$.

references.locator: Printed pp. 67–69, partial trace and reduced states; Theorem 2.22, printed pp. 82–84, finite Choi, Kraus, and Stinespring characterizations.

items.physical_scope: A finite-dimensional non-relativistic quantum system and finite environment with a fixed product initial assignment and a declared joint unitary family. A time-homogeneous finite GKSL model is an optional, separately adopted approximation. No initial system-environment correlations, continuum reservoir limit, microscopic Markov derivation, apparatus realization, or experimental observation is asserted.

items.title: Product-state reduced evolution is a channel
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement: In the finite product-state model, fix any $t\geq0$ and define the complex-linear map $\Phi_t:M_d(\mathbb C)\to M_d(\mathbb C)$ by $\Phi_t(X)=\operatorname{Tr}_E\!\left(U_t(X\otimes\eta)U_t^*\right)$. Then $\Phi_t$ is a finite quantum channel. The family $t\mapsto\Phi_t$ need not obey the semigroup law and need not be CP-divisible. The terms “semigroup law” and “CP-divisible” have the definitions of [[def-nrqmx-finite-channel-families]].

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, Chapter 2, §§2.1.3 and 2.2.2
references.locator: Printed pp. 67–69, finite partial trace; Theorem 2.22, printed pp. 82–84, finite Kraus and Stinespring forms.

references.title: Lin Lin and Nathan Wiebe, Quantum Algorithms for Scientific Computation, Chapter 21, §21.1
references.locator: Printed pp. 307–311, equations (21.1)–(21.5), Example 21.1, and the complete proof of Theorem 21.2.

items.physical_scope: Exact reduced maps of finite-dimensional system and environment models with a fixed product initial assignment and unitary joint evolution. The theorem permits neither an initial-correlation extension nor a continuum bath or Markov limit; its finite example is a conditional model calculation, not an experiment.

items.title: Amplitude damping with operational time units
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement: For the separately selected qubit GKSL model, let $H=\hbar\omega|1\rangle\langle1|$ with $\omega\in\mathbb R$ in $\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ and $\hbar>0$ in joule-seconds, and let $L=\sqrt{\gamma}|0\rangle\langle1|$ with $\gamma\geq0$ in $\mathrm{s}^{-1}$, so $L$ has units $\mathrm{s}^{-1/2}$. For any initial density matrix $\rho(0)$ in the ordered basis $(|0\rangle,|1\rangle)$, the solution $\rho(t)=e^{t\mathcal L}\rho(0)$ for $t\geq0$ satisfies $\rho_{11}(t)=e^{-\gamma t}\rho_{11}(0)$, $\rho_{00}(t)=\rho_{00}(0)+(1-e^{-\gamma t})\rho_{11}(0)$, $\rho_{01}(t)=e^{(i\omega-\gamma/2)t}\rho_{01}(0)$, and $\rho_{10}(t)=e^{(-i\omega-\gamma/2)t}\rho_{10}(0)$.

references.title: Lin Lin and Nathan Wiebe, Quantum Algorithms for Scientific Computation, Chapter 21, §21.1
references.locator: Equations (21.1)–(21.5), printed pp. 307–308, and Theorem 21.2, printed pp. 309–311: finite GKSL channel semigroups.

items.physical_scope: The exact finite-dimensional qubit time-homogeneous GKSL model with one amplitude-damping jump operator. The formulas are conditional model predictions; no vacuum continuum, reservoir limit, detector record, or empirical decay rate is asserted.

items.title: Finite jump expansion and ensemble equation
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $d\geq1$, let $H=H^*\in M_d(\mathbb C)$ have units joules, let $\hbar>0$ have units joule-seconds, and let $L_1,\ldots,L_r\in M_d(\mathbb C)$ be a finite family with units $\mathrm{s}^{-1/2}$, where $r\geq0$. For the selected time-homogeneous finite GKSL model, put $\mathcal L(X)=-\frac{i}{\hbar}[H,X]+\sum_{a=1}^r(L_aXL_a^*-\frac12\{L_a^*L_a,X\})$. With $K=-iH/\hbar-\frac12\sum_aL_a^*L_a$ and the finite branch operators of [[def-nrqmx-finite-jump-trajectories]], each no-jump operator $R(u)=e^{uK}$ is a contraction, each branch state $W_{\mathbf a,\mathbf s}(t)\rho W_{\mathbf a,\mathbf s}(t)^*$ is positive for $\rho\geq0$, and for every density matrix $\rho$ and $t\geq0$,

$$e^{t\mathcal L}(\rho)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\ \sum_{\mathbf a\in\{1,\ldots,r\}^n}\ \int_{0<s_1<\cdots<s_n<t}W_{\mathbf a,\mathbf s}(t)\rho W_{\mathbf a,\mathbf s}(t)^*\,ds_1\cdots ds_n,$$

where the $n=0$ term is $R(t)\rho R(t)^*$ and branches with $n\geq1$ are absent when $r=0$. The series converges in trace norm, uniformly on each bounded time interval; the sum of all branch weights is one. This is an ensemble representation of the finite GKSL solution, not a unique microscopic trajectory or a claim about a particular detector.

references.title: Lin Lin and Nathan Wiebe, Quantum Algorithms for Scientific Computation, Chapter 21, §21.1
references.locator: Equation (21.1), printed p. 307, for the finite GKSL generator and jump operators; the ordered finite-time branch expansion is derived locally.

items.physical_scope: The exact finite-dimensional time-homogeneous GKSL approximation with finitely many bounded jump matrices. The jump expansion is one mathematical ensemble representation; it is not asserted to be unique, to identify an actual measurement record, or to arise from a microscopic reservoir.

title: Finite reduced dynamics, memory and quantum trajectories — Examples

items.title: A finite bath revives coherence
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement: For $H_S=H_E=\mathbb C^2$, $Z=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$, $g>0$ in $\mathrm{s}^{-1}$, and $\hbar>0$ in joule-seconds, choose $H_{\mathrm{tot}}=\hbar g\,Z\otimes Z$, $U_t=e^{-itH_{\mathrm{tot}}/\hbar}$, and the fixed environment state $|+\rangle\langle+|$ with $|+\rangle=(|0\rangle+|1\rangle)/\sqrt2$ in the displayed environment $Z$ eigenbasis. Here coherence means an off-diagonal matrix entry in the displayed system basis. The reduced map leaves the system populations unchanged and multiplies each coherence by $\cos(2gt)$. At a positive time $s$ where the multiplier is zero, it erases the distinction between the two $X$ eigenstates; at $2s$ it restores them with their signs exchanged. Thus this finite reduced family is neither a semigroup nor CP-divisible.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, Chapter 2, §§2.1.3 and 2.2.2
references.locator: Printed pp. 67–69 and Theorem 2.22, printed pp. 82–84: finite reduced states and channels.

references.title: Lin Lin and Nathan Wiebe, Quantum Algorithms for Scientific Computation, Chapter 21, §21.1
references.locator: Printed pp. 307–311: finite GKSL dynamics and channel semigroups, used as comparison model context.

items.physical_scope: A conditional two-qubit finite-environment unitary model with fixed product preparation. The coherence revival is an exact model prediction, not a reported experiment or a general claim about finite reservoirs.

items.title: Single excitation jump law
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; readiness recorded separately.
items.statement: In the normalized jump-branch ensemble for the finite amplitude-damping model, let $\gamma\geq0$ be in $\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ and take the initial qubit state $|1\rangle\langle1|$. The no-jump survival weight at time $t\geq0$ is $e^{-\gamma t}$. If $\gamma>0$, the ensemble assigns the first-jump time density $\gamma e^{-\gamma t}$ and post-jump state $|0\rangle\langle0|$; because there is no drive and $L|0\rangle=0$, there are no later jumps. If $\gamma=0$, no jump occurs and the survival weight is one. This is a model branch distribution, not a detector observation.

references.title: Lin Lin and Nathan Wiebe, Quantum Algorithms for Scientific Computation, Chapter 21, §21.1
references.locator: Equation (21.1), printed p. 307, and Theorem 21.2, printed pp. 309–311: finite GKSL jump operators and channel dynamics.

items.physical_scope: An ideal trajectory-ensemble calculation for an undriven qubit in the finite amplitude-damping GKSL model. It predicts a model waiting-time law and state update; it is not a reported detector observation.
